name: Inghean Bhuidhe

attributes.attribute: an Irish goddess whose name means the yellow-haired girl, one of three goddesses of Munster
Christianized into a saint and honored on May 6 with rituals at a sacred well
the sister of Inghean Bhuidhe, a fire deity whose name means red claw

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Inghean Bhuidhe is an Irish goddess. The name means the yellow-haired girl. She is one of three related goddesses in the southwestern province of Munster. Her sister Latiaran appears to have been an ancient fire goddess. Another sister was Crobh Dearg, or red claw, perhaps another fire deity. Some tellers name the third sister Lasair. The Christian church made Inghean Bhuidhe a saint. People honored her on May 6 with rituals at a sacred well. She is an obscure figure. Her worship stayed inside a small geographical region. Little legend describes her powers.
